# Generic engine: posterior-propagated outcome model

Fits a model once, then refits on a fresh posterior draw of the OUTCOME on
every iteration `k` (same pattern as `run_mother_eigen_mediation_bayesian_joint`
/ `run_juvenile_mediation_bayesian_joint_eigen` elsewhere in this pipeline).
Returns every MCMC sample from every draw `k` pooled together, so downstream
summaries reflect both (a) uncertainty in each male's own network-position
estimate and (b) ordinary model/parameter uncertainty - not just the
posterior mean plugged in as if it were observed without error.

```{r engine}
run_posterior_outcome_model <- function(data, id_col, posteriors, field, formula_rhs,
                                         num_draws = 1000, chains = 2, iter = 2000,
                                         warmup = 1000, adapt_delta = 0.95) {

  ids_with_post <- data[[id_col]][data[[id_col]] %in% names(posteriors)]
  dat <- data %>% filter(.data[[id_col]] %in% ids_with_post)

  if (nrow(dat) < 10) stop("Too few individuals with posteriors (n = ", nrow(dat), ")")

  actual_draws <- length(posteriors[[dat[[id_col]][1]]][[field]])
  num_draws <- min(num_draws, actual_draws)

  build_draw_data <- function(k) {
    dat_k <- dat
    dat_k$outcome <- sapply(dat_k[[id_col]], function(id) posteriors[[id]][[field]][k])
    dat_k
  }

  dat_1 <- build_draw_data(1)
  f <- bf(as.formula(paste0("outcome ~ ", formula_rhs)))

  cat("  Compiling model (draw 1) for outcome field:", field, "...\n")
  fit_base <- brm(f, data = dat_1, family = gaussian(),
                   chains = chains, iter = iter, warmup = warmup, seed = 1,
                   refresh = 0, silent = 2, control = list(adapt_delta = adapt_delta))

  all_draws <- list(as_draws_df(fit_base))

  for (k in 2:num_draws) {
    dat_k <- build_draw_data(k)
    fit_k <- update(fit_base, newdata = dat_k, recompile = FALSE, refresh = 0, silent = 2)
    all_draws[[k]] <- as_draws_df(fit_k)
  }

  list(n = nrow(dat), num_draws = num_draws, pooled = bind_rows(all_draws))
}
```

# Test 1: Natal group identity -> maternal rank & sons' pre-dispersal behaviour

Variance-partitioning (ICC) via a random intercept on `BirthGp`: what
fraction of variance in each outcome is attributable to which natal group
a male was born into.

Restricted to the same N=33 males used in the actual mediation analyses
(non-missing `mother_avg_elo` AND `elo_one_year_male_male`, matching Table
S3's sample) rather than the broader population - the point here is to
check whether the mediation *results* are confounded by natal group, not
to characterize natal-group effects across all males more generally.
This same N=33 core sample is also used for Test 2 below.

```{r icc-sample}
# Core mediation sample - just the rank-mediation criterion, no BirthGp
# constraint, so it can be reused for Test 2 (which doesn't use BirthGp)
# without natal-group-specific filtering leaking in.
mediation_sample_codes <- emigrants_full %>%
  filter(!is.na(mother_avg_elo), !is.na(elo_one_year_male_male)) %>%
  pull(Code)

cat("Core mediation sample size:", length(mediation_sample_codes), "\n")

# Test 1's version adds the natal-group-specific filters on top
emigrants_full_icc <- emigrants_full %>%
  filter(Code %in% mediation_sample_codes, !is.na(BirthGp), BirthGp != "CR")

cat("Test 1 (natal group) sample size:", nrow(emigrants_full_icc), "\n")
cat("Natal groups represented:", paste(sort(unique(emigrants_full_icc$BirthGp)), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## 1a. Fixed-value outcomes (maternal rank)

Maternal rank is a genuinely observed value, not a posterior distribution,
so a single ordinary fit is correct here - no draw-loop needed.

```{r test1a-fixed}
fit_natal_group_icc_fixed <- function(outcome, data) {
  f <- bf(as.formula(paste0(outcome, " ~ 1 + (1 | BirthGp)")))
  fit <- brm(f, data = data, family = gaussian(),
             chains = 2, iter = 2000, warmup = 1000, seed = 1,
             refresh = 0, silent = 2, control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99))
  draws <- as_draws_df(fit)
  icc <- draws$sd_BirthGp__Intercept^2 / (draws$sd_BirthGp__Intercept^2 + draws$sigma^2)
  tibble(outcome = outcome, n = nrow(data), icc_mean = mean(icc), icc_median = median(icc),
         icc_q025 = quantile(icc, 0.025), icc_q975 = quantile(icc, 0.975))
}

natal_group_results_fixed <- fit_natal_group_icc_fixed("mother_avg_elo", emigrants_full_icc)
print(natal_group_results_fixed)
```

print(natal_group_results_fixed)

## 1a-extended. Other maternal characteristics (point-estimate ICC)

Same fixed-value approach as above, extended to the other four maternal
variables (investment and eigen-centrality). Uses point-estimate posterior
means (`mom_groom_eigen_mean`/`mom_prox_eigen_mean`) rather than full
posterior propagation - a tractability tradeoff, consistent with how
`mother_avg_elo` above is already treated as a fixed value.

```{r test1a-maternal-extended}
maternal_icc_fields <- c(
  "mom_groom_proportion",
  "mom_prox_proportion",
  "mom_groom_eigen_mean",
  "mom_prox_eigen_mean"
)

natal_group_results_maternal <- bind_rows(lapply(maternal_icc_fields, function(outcome) {
  if (!outcome %in% names(emigrants_full_icc)) {
    message("Column '", outcome, "' not found - skipping")
    return(NULL)
  }
  cat("Fitting natal-group ICC for:", outcome, "\n")
  fit_natal_group_icc_fixed(
    outcome,
    emigrants_full_icc %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[outcome]]))
  )
}))

print(natal_group_results_maternal)

write.csv(natal_group_results_maternal,
          file.path(data_dir, "natal_group_icc_results_maternal.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

## 1b. Posterior-outcome juvenile network metrics

Each son's network position is itself a distribution, drawn from
`groom_posteriors_juv` / `prox_posteriors_juv` (the same objects loaded in
script 10). Uses the generic engine above so uncertainty in each son's own
network-position estimate propagates into the ICC.

```{r test1b-load-posteriors}
groom_posteriors_juv <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "groom_posteriors_juvenile.rds"))
prox_posteriors_juv  <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "prox_posteriors_juvenile.rds"))

# Confirm the $field names below actually match what's stored, e.g.:
# names(groom_posteriors_juv[[1]])
# names(prox_posteriors_juv[[1]])
```

```{r test1b-run}
juvenile_icc_fields <- list(
  list(posteriors = groom_posteriors_juv, field = "groom_in_strength_juv",  label = "groom_in_strength_juv"),
  list(posteriors = groom_posteriors_juv, field = "groom_out_strength_juv", label = "groom_out_strength_juv"),
  list(posteriors = groom_posteriors_juv, field = "groom_in_degree_juv",    label = "groom_in_degree_juv"),
  list(posteriors = groom_posteriors_juv, field = "groom_out_degree_juv",   label = "groom_out_degree_juv"),
  list(posteriors = prox_posteriors_juv,  field = "prox_strength_juv",      label = "prox_strength_juv"),
  list(posteriors = prox_posteriors_juv,  field = "prox_degree_juv",        label = "prox_degree_juv")
)
# NOTE: adjust field names above if they differ from what test1b-load-posteriors
# confirmed. Set eval=TRUE once confirmed - left off by default since this
# runs ~1000 brms refits per outcome (6 outcomes here), same scale as one
# of your existing mediation-analysis chunks.

natal_group_results_posterior <- bind_rows(lapply(juvenile_icc_fields, function(spec) {
  cat("Fitting natal-group ICC (posterior-propagated) for:", spec$label, "\n")
  res <- run_posterior_outcome_model(
    data = emigrants_full_icc,
    id_col = "Code", posteriors = spec$posteriors, field = spec$field,
    formula_rhs = "1 + (1 | BirthGp)", num_draws = 1000
  )
  icc <- res$pooled$sd_BirthGp__Intercept^2 /
    (res$pooled$sd_BirthGp__Intercept^2 + res$pooled$sigma^2)
  tibble(outcome = spec$label, n = res$n, num_draws = res$num_draws,
         icc_mean = mean(icc), icc_median = median(icc),
         icc_q025 = quantile(icc, 0.025), icc_q975 = quantile(icc, 0.975))
}))
print(natal_group_results_posterior)

write.csv(bind_rows(natal_group_results_fixed, natal_group_results_posterior),
          file.path(data_dir, "natal_group_icc_results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Test 2: Immigration group size / sex ratio at dispersal -> male rank & post-dispersal behaviour

Continuous covariates (group size, sex ratio at immigration) rather than
group x year identity - tests the actual size/sex-ratio hypothesis instead
of an unidentifiable near-singleton categorical term.

**Note:** `median_group_size` (already in `emigrants_full`) is the median
size of each male's *natal* group during his *juvenile* window (computed in
script 8) - it does not answer this question, which is about the
*destination* group at the moment of immigration. No sex-ratio column
exists anywhere in `emigrants_full`. Both are built fresh below from
`group_presence_matrices.rds` (presence, columns = individual `Code`) joined
to `life_history.csv`'s `Sex` column.

## 2.0 Extract group size and sex ratio at each male's immigration date

```{r test2-extract-context}
group_presence_matrices <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "group_presence_matrices.rds"))
life_hist <- read.csv("/Users/alba/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Postdoc_UNIL/Vervet_projects/IVP_data/life_history.csv")

# Presence matrix columns are lowercase Codes (script 1 does this before
# building the matrices: life_hist$Code <- tolower(life_hist$Code)) -
# apply the same transformation here so the join actually matches.
life_hist$Code <- tolower(life_hist$Code)

sex_lookup <- life_hist %>% distinct(Code, Sex)

# For a given group + date, returns list(group_size, sex_ratio) where
# sex_ratio = n_females / n_males among everyone present that day (all
# ages, not adult-restricted - see note below if you want adults only).
get_group_context <- function(group_name, target_date, presence_matrices, sex_lookup,
                               max_date_gap = 7) {
  if (is.na(group_name) || is.na(target_date) || !group_name %in% names(presence_matrices)) {
    return(list(group_size = NA_real_, sex_ratio = NA_real_))
  }
  pm <- presence_matrices[[group_name]]
  pm$Date <- as.Date(pm$Date)

  row <- pm %>% filter(Date == as.Date(target_date))
  if (nrow(row) == 0) {
    # fall back to nearest available date within max_date_gap days
    pm_near <- pm %>% mutate(gap = abs(as.numeric(Date - as.Date(target_date)))) %>%
      filter(gap <= max_date_gap) %>% arrange(gap)
    if (nrow(pm_near) == 0) return(list(group_size = NA_real_, sex_ratio = NA_real_))
    row <- pm_near[1, ]
  }

  present_codes <- names(row)[-1][as.logical(as.numeric(row[1, -1]))]
  present_codes <- setdiff(present_codes, c("gap"))  # in case fallback row carries it

  sexes <- sex_lookup$Sex[match(present_codes, sex_lookup$Code)]
  n_f <- sum(sexes == "F", na.rm = TRUE)
  n_m <- sum(sexes == "M", na.rm = TRUE)

  if (n_f == 0 && n_m == 0 && length(present_codes) > 0) {
    warning("Sex lookup matched 0 of ", length(present_codes),
            " present individuals for group ", group_name, " - check Code format")
  }

  list(group_size = length(present_codes),
       sex_ratio = if (n_m > 0) n_f / n_m else NA_real_)
}

emigrants_full <- emigrants_full %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    context = list(get_group_context(ImmigrationGp1, DateImmigration1,
                                      group_presence_matrices, sex_lookup)),
    group_size_at_immigration = context$group_size,
    sex_ratio_at_immigration  = context$sex_ratio
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-context)

cat("group_size_at_immigration coverage:", sum(!is.na(emigrants_full$group_size_at_immigration)), "/", nrow(emigrants_full), "\n")
cat("sex_ratio_at_immigration coverage:", sum(!is.na(emigrants_full$sex_ratio_at_immigration)), "/", nrow(emigrants_full), "\n")
summary(emigrants_full$group_size_at_immigration)
summary(emigrants_full$sex_ratio_at_immigration)
```

This computes `sex_ratio_at_immigration` as females-per-male among
*everyone present* that day (all ages) - a simpler, immediately-computable
version. If you want it restricted to *adults only* (matching the
`get_age_class()` AM/AF logic already used in script 1), that needs each
present individual's age at that date too - say the word and I'll extend
this to reuse that classification.

## 2a. Fixed-value outcome (post-dispersal rank)

```{r test2a-fixed}
fit_dispersal_context_fixed <- function(outcome, data, predictors) {
  predictors <- predictors[predictors %in% names(data)]
  if (length(predictors) == 0) stop("None of the requested predictor columns were found")
  f <- bf(as.formula(paste0(outcome, " ~ ", paste(predictors, collapse = " + "))))
  brm(f, data = data, family = gaussian(), chains = 2, iter = 2000, warmup = 1000,
      seed = 1, refresh = 0, silent = 2, control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95))
}

fit_rank_context <- fit_dispersal_context_fixed(
  "elo_one_year_male_male",
  emigrants_full %>% filter(Code %in% mediation_sample_codes),
  predictors = c("group_size_at_immigration", "sex_ratio_at_immigration")
)
summary(fit_rank_context)
```

scale reduction factor on split chains (at convergence, Rhat = 1).

## 2b. Posterior-outcome: post-dispersal network metrics (all six)

Uses the same engine as Test 1b, with the ADULT posteriors
(`prox_posteriors.rds` / `groom_posteriors.rds`) as the outcome, regressed
on group size / sex ratio at immigration - looped across every network
metric rather than just `prox_strength`.

```{r test2b-posterior}
prox_posteriors  <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "prox_posteriors.rds"))
groom_posteriors <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "groom_posteriors.rds"))

# Confirm these field names match what's actually stored before trusting
# the loop below, same caveat as Test 1b:
# names(prox_posteriors[[1]]); names(groom_posteriors[[1]])
adult_network_fields <- list(
  list(posteriors = prox_posteriors,  field = "prox_strength",       label = "prox_strength"),
  list(posteriors = prox_posteriors,  field = "prox_degree",         label = "prox_degree"),
  list(posteriors = groom_posteriors, field = "groom_in_strength",   label = "groom_in_strength"),
  list(posteriors = groom_posteriors, field = "groom_out_strength",  label = "groom_out_strength"),
  list(posteriors = groom_posteriors, field = "groom_in_degree",     label = "groom_in_degree"),
  list(posteriors = groom_posteriors, field = "groom_out_degree",    label = "groom_out_degree")
)
# NOTE: this runs ~1000 brms refits per outcome (6 outcomes) - same scale
# as Test 1b and one of your existing mediation-analysis chunks.

dispersal_context_results <- bind_rows(lapply(adult_network_fields, function(spec) {
  cat("Fitting dispersal-context model for:", spec$label, "\n")
  res <- run_posterior_outcome_model(
    data = emigrants_full %>% filter(Code %in% mediation_sample_codes), id_col = "Code",
    posteriors = spec$posteriors, field = spec$field,
    formula_rhs = "group_size_at_immigration + sex_ratio_at_immigration",
    num_draws = 1000
  )
  tibble(
    outcome = spec$label,
    term = c("group_size_at_immigration", "sex_ratio_at_immigration"),
    n = res$n, num_draws = res$num_draws,
    mean = c(mean(res$pooled$b_group_size_at_immigration), mean(res$pooled$b_sex_ratio_at_immigration)),
    q025 = c(quantile(res$pooled$b_group_size_at_immigration, .025), quantile(res$pooled$b_sex_ratio_at_immigration, .025)),
    q975 = c(quantile(res$pooled$b_group_size_at_immigration, .975), quantile(res$pooled$b_sex_ratio_at_immigration, .975))
  )
}))
print(dispersal_context_results, n = Inf)

write.csv(dispersal_context_results,
          file.path(data_dir, "dispersal_context_network_results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```
